newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures end lower, await US 4Q cost index.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures end lower, await US 4Q cost index.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended lower, but climbed off session lows on light short-covering after March T-bonds failed to break below a 2-1/2-month low, traders and analysts said.
The contract verged on knocking through 109-26/32, which is also the lower end of the market's 2-1/2-week range, on concerns about Tuesday's U.S. fourth-quarter employment cost index report.
Traders have been discussing the cost index all week on expectations that the data will reveal whether or not health care costs are contributing to rising U.S. wage pressures.

March T-bonds looked ready to break to 109-26/32 at midsession when the contract fell to 110-06/32, the two-week low, and then quickly fell to 109-28/32. One large, prominent pit trader sold about 2,000 contracts from 110-06/32 to 109-28/32.
"It's a wholesale sell off at this point," one bond futures trader said.

Traders said selling pressure in the 10-year note pit spilled into the bond pit. One trader sold about 700 March 10-year note contracts, while another fund was reportedly a large seller of five-year notes in the cash markets.
Some traders said the market was poised to head lower at the start of the day, as several firms were buying the June bond contract and selling March.
They also said pressures ahead of the expiration of February bond options were building up to the downside, noting that open interest in puts totaled about 24,000.
March bonds initially held support at 110-09/32, but declines in the U.S. stock market festered in the bond pit and contributed to the bearish mood.
Traders were watching stocks like "hawks," and said the bond market remained vulnerable to any moves in stock prices.

June Eurodollars fell through support at 94.15, while September Eurodollars eased near support at the 93.94 level. Traders noted little flight-to-quality buying from U.S. stocks into the short-end of the debt market.
In fact, many Eurodollar traders believe stocks will continue to post record highs, and possibly give the Federal Reserve a reason to tighten U.S. interest rates.
"Eurodollars are not acting confidently," one analyst said. "It's related to the strength in housing, autos and stocks in the last year."

At the end of pit trade, March T-bonds were down 19/32 at 110-08/32, 10-year notes were off 10/32 at 107-31/32, June Eurodollars were down one basis point at 94.18, September Eurodollars were off two bps at 93.99, and June T-bills were one bps lower at 94.74.
